name: French Toast
label: Dischord
lede: James Canty and Jerry Busher had spent twenty years in the same D.C. rooms without sharing a band. Once they did, they traded guitar, bass, drums and keys song by song and sounded like a crowd.

eras.title: Friends for twenty years, a band for one
eras.text: Canty came up through Nation of Ulysses and The Make-Up; Busher toured with Fugazi for eight years. In 2001 they finally made their own band, and their first records came out on the small Arrest Records, not Dischord.

years.cap: James Canty on guitar at Pianos, New York, December 2003
years.h: After twenty years of friendship, Canty and Busher start a band
years.p: Dischord says [[James Canty|ffc732f4-15a3-42e1-a498-965c1d793e35]] and [[Jerry Busher|59c39d46-efd2-4fa0-912e-93ead7a4ab97]] had known each other for more than two decades without ever sharing a band. Canty came from Nation of Ulysses and the Make-Up; Busher from [[Fidelity Jones|c6332c9e-a2e3-4d2d-8ad7-a6b3ee837717]] and Fugazi.
years.xp:
Busher started with Fugazi as a roadie and ended up on drums, percussion and trumpet in its live shows; he is on The Argument (2001). Canty drummed in Nation of Ulysses before switching to guitar and organ in the Make-Up.

French Toast was built for two people who could play everything. Both sang, both played keys, and guitar, bass and drums went to whoever the song needed.

years.cap: Jerry Busher on drums at Pianos, New York, December 2003
years.h: Bug Man comes out on Arrest Records, not Dischord
years.p: The duo's first release is Arrest catalog number are01, three years before they reach Dischord.

yt: Live at the Ottobar, Baltimore, March 13, 2004
years.h: A second single, Hatred Mace / For Sylvia, keeps the duo going
years.p: Also on Arrest Records (are03), it arrives while the debut album is still being made.

eras.title: Dischord gets a duo that sounds like a crowd
eras.text: French Toast reached Dischord in 2005 with a debut that didn't sound like the label's reputation: dub, samples, horns and angular funk under sharp guitars. Before the year was out the two-piece had a third member.

yt: Live at the Khyber, Philadelphia, April 16, 2005
years.h: In a Cave arrives as Dischord No. 148
years.p: Twelve songs, co-produced with Bill Skibble and Jessica Ruffins at Key Club Recording Studios, with Canty and Busher splitting the vocals and every instrument.
years.xp: It came out on CD and on 180-gram vinyl. Months earlier, on April 16, the duo played the Khyber in Philadelphia, where a fan filmed the set.

years.p: The paper runs the review in its July 1 edition, a notice most first albums on a small label never get.

years.cap: French Toast live at Magnet Club, Berlin, June 22, 2006
years.h: Ben Gilligan joins and the duo becomes a trio
years.p: Dischord says the multi-instrumentalist came in late 2005 on bass, guitar and vocals. Now three people swapped instruments on stage instead of two.

eras.title: The last record, made with family
eras.text: The trio toured, put out a second Dischord album with Canty's brother at the controls, and then stopped.

years.big: There's a lot of sharing going on
years.h: Chicago previews the Empty Bottle show with Supersystem
years.p: French Toast open for [[Supersystem|b900616e-fd32-4c17-8f77-17ae2f1413a0]] on January 12. Oh My Rockness says the band sounds more like angular funk than aggressive punk, with dub, samples and horns.
years.xp:
The Chicago listings site ran the preview on January 5 under the headline "French Toast are not your typical Dischord band." It still finds the label's marks in them: sharp guitars and atypical rhythms.

On the instruments, it notes Busher plays bass, drums, vocals and keyboards, and that the members trade roles.

years.p: The first record as a trio, produced by [[Brendan Canty|8b505ef0-c5a7-4deb-bc32-27c882f3c40e]], James Canty's brother and Busher's old Fugazi bandmate.
years.xp:
Recorded at Blindspot Studios and The Cave; [[T.J. Lipple|ed4cd729-b4d2-4016-a0b6-c362b68d2afb]] mastered it at Silver Sonya.

The credits show how loose the jobs were: Jerry Busher is listed on vocals, guitar, bass, drums, tapes and keys; James Canty on vocals, guitar and organ; Ben Gilligan on vocals, guitar and bass. Twelve songs, including one called Brejnev and a closer called Fork in the Road.

years.cap: French Toast as a trio at Magnet Club, Berlin, June 22, 2006
years.h: After Ingleside Terrace, French Toast is done
years.p: Dischord lists it as the second and final full-length. The band parted ways in 2006, five years after it started.

eras.title: Everybody's go-to players
eras.text: The band ended, but Canty and Busher kept doing what they'd always done: turning up in other people's bands and improving them. Busher eventually landed in Scream, one of the first D.C. hardcore bands.

years.h: Canty takes guitar duty in [[Ted Leo and the Pharmacists|31095622-5a1e-4f22-8ad1-b08eb6255f37]]
years.p: He's known as a guitarist in Ted Leo's band, and in 2008 records the digital EP Rapid Response with them, a benefit for Democracy Now! and Food Not Bombs.

years.h: Busher drums for D.C. Afrobeat band Funk Ark
years.p: The D.C. Afrobeat and funk outfit is one of the bands Jerry Busher plays in after French Toast.

years.h: Busher takes the drum stool in [[Deathfix|db0e5c06-c091-46d4-bd42-5ba2ee299123]]
years.p: He replaces Devin Ocampo in Brendan Canty's band, putting two Fugazi alumni back in a room.

years.h: Canty fills in on keys for Late Night with Seth Meyers
years.p: James Canty becomes the show's fill-in keyboardist.
Wikipedia credits Jerry Busher on drums and percussion with the early D.C. hardcore band from 2023 into 2024.
